bib.title: 9. Deployment: Launching Your AI Application into Production | Learning LangChain

question: How do you deploy a LangChain/LangGraph retrieval-agent application to production, with a vector store, backend API, monitoring and basic security?
contributions: Walkthrough deploying a template retrieval agent using Supabase (pgvector), LangSmith and LangGraph Platform
Description of the LangGraph Platform API data models and features
Security guidance for agents: limit permissions, anticipate misuse, defense in depth, abuse and cost controls

results.claim: A LangGraph Platform Production deployment is stated to serve up to 500 requests/second with highly available storage and automatic backups.
results.setup: Production development type on LangGraph Platform; vendor capability statement, no benchmark or hardware given

results.claim: The documents table uses 1536-dimension vectors, matching OpenAI embeddings.
results.setup: Supabase pgvector table in the example; change if the embedding model differs
results.quote: embedding vector(1536) -- 1536 works for OpenAI embeddings

results.claim: The Platform API supports five streaming modes (values, messages, updates, events, debug).
results.quote: Platform API supports five streaming modes:

results.claim: Four double-texting strategies are offered: reject, enqueue, interrupt, rollback.
results.quote: LangGraph Platform provides four different solutions to handle double

results.claim: The local langgraph-cli requires Python 3.11 or higher.
results.setup: Local dev server via langgraph dev

results.claim: Agents should be given least-privilege credentials, assumed to be usable in any way the permissions allow, with layered defenses such as read-only credentials plus sandboxing.
results.quote: Always assume that any system access or credentials may be used

results.claim: To limit abuse and cost, add account verification, rate limiting in middleware, and prompt-injection guardrails (permission scoping and strict prompts).
Stateless background runs restart from scratch if the worker dies halfway.
results.quote: the entire run will be retried from scratch

limits: Product tutorial for a specific vendor stack (LangGraph Platform, LangSmith Plus, Supabase); UI steps and pricing tiers date quickly.
No measurements, benchmarks, cost or latency numbers; the 500 requests/second figure is an unsupported vendor statement.
Monitoring is only a few sentences on LangSmith dashboards; testing, evaluation and benchmarking are deferred to Chapter 10.
Security advice is brief and generic, with no testing of prompt-injection defenses.
Code listings are partly truncated in the extracted text (JavaScript snippets, SQL function).
practices: Run the app locally with `langgraph dev` and test via cURL and the SDK before deploying (Test Your LangGraph App Locally).
Place langgraph.json at or above the files holding compiled graphs; set dependencies, graphs and env (Create a LangGraph API Config).
Mark sensitive environment variables such as OPENAI_API_KEY as Secret in the deployment form (Environment variables).
Use Supabase pgvector with a match_documents function (cosine similarity, metadata filter, match_count limit) as the vector store.
Insert human-in-the-loop checkpoints where logic invokes tools or accesses specific documents (Human-in-the-loop).
Limit agent permissions, assume misuse, and layer defenses (Security).
For file, API and database access, scope to a directory, use read-only keys, scope credentials to needed tables (Security examples).
Add account verification, rate limiting and prompt-injection guardrails to control abuse and cost (Security).
